verifications.note: Reproduced on the round-5 candidate d141d303: check_test_refs.py reports 5 T4 problems and exits 1. On the round-6 candidate a059b55 it reports '52 declared test titles derived from 3 test files; 42 quoted test title citation(s) in 411 register rows; 0 problem(s)' and exits 0. The fix removes the hand-maintained EXPECTED_TITLES list and derives the titles from the test files: JS test(...) literals and Python def test_* methods. It adds sound T4 derivation checks (JS call count equals literal titles, every test file yields titles, no duplicate titles) and a built-in T5 negative control. I checked the fix with my own mutations in a disposable copy. Renaming a cited JS title gives a T1 problem and exit 1 (REQ-DLV-022). Renaming a cited Python test gives a T1 problem and exit 1 (REQ-DLV-013). Adding a test with a non-literal title gives a T4 problem and exit 1. The clean copy exits 0. The five round-4 tests and the five run_meta unit tests are now cited in REQ-DLV-013/016/021/022/026, and every cited title exists and passes (unittest: 5 tests OK). prefreeze.sh now runs every docs/analysis/tools check. The fix is complete. Separately, prefreeze.sh itself fails on the candidate because of committed .pyc files; that is a new, unrelated defect, recorded as F-DG0-010.
